prompt: Build "Gummy Bears" - a single self-contained HTML file (relying only on three.js from CDN): a small handful of translucent gummy bears on a white table that you can grab, stretch, squish, throw, and dump. Gummy Bears - classic gummy bear silhouette: round head with two ears, short muzzle, chubby body, stubby arms and legs, small molded eyes and nose - each part smoothly melting into the next - build body as implicit surfaces (metaballs / marching cubes), not separate spheres - Material: realistic gummy candy. Translucent with transmission and refraction, color light absorption deeper in thick parts, glossy lacquer with sharp highlights - Colors: cherry red, orange, lemon yellow, apple green, clear pineapple - soft colored shadow under each bear, tinted by the bear's own color. Physics (this is the whole point - must feel like jelly, not plastic) - each bear is a soft body: mass points for head, ears, muzzle, body, belly, hands, and feet connected via volume-preserving shape matching - limbs and neck rendered as stretchable chains between points that thin when pulled - grab any part and pull: it stretches like rubber, the rest of the bear tilts along, snaps back with damped wobble on release - pull head upward: neck stretches, body follows, releases into squash and jump - press head downward: bear squashes like a pancake, bulges laterally, springs back up - throw a bear: it flies, squashes on landing, bounces, and shoves other bears - bears collide with each other, never pass through - idle bears do small random hops with squash and stretch - "Pour more bears" drops a handful from above into a wobbly, jiggling pile. UI - editorial product page style, white background. Large italic serif header "Gummy / Bears.", a short subhead, a minimalist card on the right with flavor swatches, a wobble slider, live "Stretch" and "Bounce" readouts, and a "Pour more bears" button - a subtle circular cursor that expands on grab - ACES tone mapping, environment reflections, soft key and rim lighting. Smooth 60fps.

post.originalText:
同一套提示词，让 Opus 5.5 和 Gemini 4 Argon 分别做了一组可以拉扯、挤压和投掷的 3D 软糖熊。

视频上面是 Opus，下面是 Gemini。

测试动作完全一样：拉手、拽头、压扁、扔出去，最后再倒一整袋软糖熊进去。

结果差距很明显。

Opus 做出来的熊更像真正的软糖：

• 拉住手臂会越扯越细，松开后还能回弹晃动  
• 压扁后会摊成一块，然后重新弹起来  
• 扔出去会撞到其他软糖熊，并把它们推开  
• 材质透明、有光泽，光线能穿过去  

Gemini 做出来的更像塑料模型：

• 手臂被拉成了一根硬棍  
• 熊会直接穿过旁边的物体  
• 多个模型堆在一起时出现明显穿模  

更意外的是价格：

Opus：$7.2  
Gemini：$22

这次比的已经不是画面好不好看，而是模型能不能理解软体材质、碰撞和物理反馈。

这一轮，Opus 赢得很明显。

sourceMaterials.text:
提示词：
  构建“Gummy Bears” - 一个单一的自包含HTML文件（仅依赖CDN上的three.js）：在白色桌子上的一小把半透明的软糖熊，你可以抓住、拉伸、挤压、扔和倾倒。  软糖熊 - 经典软糖熊轮廓：圆形头部带两个耳朵，短吻，丰满的身体，粗短的手臂和腿部，小型模压眼睛和鼻子 - 每个部分平滑融化到下一个部分 - 将身体构建为隐式表面（元球 / 行进立方体），而不是单独的球体 - 材质：真实的软糖果。半透明，具有透射和折射，颜色光吸收在厚实部分更深，光泽清漆带有锐利的亮点 - 颜色：樱桃红、橙色、柠檬黄、苹果绿、透明菠萝 - 每个熊下方柔和的有色阴影，由熊自身的颜色着色  物理效果（这是整个重点 - 必须感觉像果冻，而不是塑料） - 每只熊是一个软体：头部、耳朵、吻、身体、腹部、手和脚的质量点，通过体积保持的形状匹配连接在一起 - 四肢和脖子渲染为点之间的可拉伸链条，拉伸时变细 - 抓住任何部分并拉动：它像橡胶一样拉伸，熊的其余部分随之倾斜，松开时它会弹回并伴随阻尼摆动 - 向上拉头部：脖子拉伸，身体跟随，松开时熊会挤压并跳跃 - 向下按压头部：熊会像煎饼一样压扁，向侧面膨胀，然后弹回向上 - 扔一只熊：它飞翔，落地时挤压，弹跳并推开其他熊 - 熊之间会碰撞，绝不会穿过彼此 - 闲置的熊会进行小型随机跳跃，伴随挤压和拉伸 - “倾倒更多熊”从上方掉下一把，落入摇晃、抖动的堆中  用户界面 - 编辑风格的产品页面风格，白色背景。大型斜体衬线标题“Gummy / Bears.”，一个简短的副标题，右侧一个最小化卡片带有口味样本，一个摇摆滑块，实时“拉伸”和“弹跳”读数，以及一个“倾倒更多熊”按钮 - 一个微妙的圆形光标，在抓取时会增大 - ACES色调映射，环境反射，柔和主光和背光。平滑60fps

translations.en: Build "Gummy Bears" - a single self-contained HTML file (relying only on three.js from CDN): a small handful of translucent gummy bears on a white table that you can grab, stretch, squish, throw, and dump. Gummy Bears - classic gummy bear silhouette: round head with two ears, short muzzle, chubby body, stubby arms and legs, small molded eyes and nose - each part smoothly melting into the next - build body as implicit surfaces (metaballs / marching cubes), not separate spheres - Material: realistic gummy candy. Translucent with transmission and refraction, color light absorption deeper in thick parts, glossy lacquer with sharp highlights - Colors: cherry red, orange, lemon yellow, apple green, clear pineapple - soft colored shadow under each bear, tinted by the bear's own color. Physics (this is the whole point - must feel like jelly, not plastic) - each bear is a soft body: mass points for head, ears, muzzle, body, belly, hands, and feet connected via volume-preserving shape matching - limbs and neck rendered as stretchable chains between points that thin when pulled - grab any part and pull: it stretches like rubber, the rest of the bear tilts along, snaps back with damped wobble on release - pull head upward: neck stretches, body follows, releases into squash and jump - press head downward: bear squashes like a pancake, bulges laterally, springs back up - throw a bear: it flies, squashes on landing, bounces, and shoves other bears - bears collide with each other, never pass through - idle bears do small random hops with squash and stretch - "Pour more bears" drops a handful from above into a wobbly, jiggling pile. UI - editorial product page style, white background. Large italic serif header "Gummy / Bears.", a short subhead, a minimalist card on the right with flavor swatches, a wobble slider, live "Stretch" and "Bounce" readouts, and a "Pour more bears" button - a subtle circular cursor that expands on grab - ACES tone mapping, environment reflections, soft key and rim lighting. Smooth 60fps.

promptValidation.evidence: The video recording shows the Opus 5.5 implementation running in a browser with the exact UI specified ('Gummy / Bears.' headline, flavor swatches, sliders, 'Pour more bears' button), demonstrating interactive soft-body stretching of arms, squishing the head, throwing, and pouring additional bears into a pile with translucent gelatinous materials and tinted shadows.
